doc.title: Catherine Russell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 26, 2018

title: Memories of her father
summary: She recalls her father practicing piano, always dressed up, making home movies including Armstrong footage, and her Panamanian upbringing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So your dad passed away, you were seven. So I’m curious if you have this process of discovery about him going on now.

Yeah. I mean I remember him then because my memory was that — one of them was that he would practice. Sit at a piano and practice classical music. And then the other one, the other two is that he was always dressed up in the house. He never walked around the house in a bathrobe or slippers or pajamas. He was always dressed up. Pants creased. He used to send his shirts to the Chinese laundry, get them back in that paper in the box. And his last job was as a chauffeur for the president of Yeshiva University in upper Manhattan, in Washington Heights. So I remembered that. And then he liked his home movies. So he had a Bell & Howell, you know, metal set up with the reels and a projector and a splicing machine. So he’d sit and splice. So we have a lot of footage of me. He’d sit and — he took a lot of the family you know — so he’d sit and splice. He’d be sitting there for hours with the razor blade and the scotch tape and he’s editing and splicing you know. And that’s where we got our footage of Louis Armstrong as well. So I remember that. I remember his friends, he had friends and I had a very kind of Panamanian/ Caribbean upbringing, so it was always good food, cooking and he was a good cook, or we’d spend time with relatives, our Panamanian family. But now, yeah. I mean, and then I remember then listening to his music also. So that was some of the first music I ever heard besides classical music, because my mother was very much into classical music and opera. And I thought wow, this sounds great. It sounds like fun. These people sing. I could kind of see the musicians in my mind or something. I imagined people just dancing to this music. But yeah, and so now, going back through his archive and everything, is very exciting. All the — because he was really in the thick of so much stuff back then.
